name: Persistent sessions with tmux or screen (Linux)
description: Make your SSH sessions survive a dropped connection, check whether a host already does, and clean up the ones you left behind. The install step is Linux only; the report and kill steps also work on macOS.
author: voltius

snippets.name: Install tmux
snippets.description: Installs tmux with whichever package manager this host has. Clears the "session will not survive disconnects" warning.

steps.content:
# Voltius wraps an SSH session in tmux (or screen) so it survives a dropped
# connection. With neither installed the session dies with the link, which is
# what the "tmux/screen not found" banner is telling you.
if command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "tmux is already installed"
else
  if   command -v apt-get >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y tmux
  elif command -v dnf     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo dnf install -y tmux
  elif command -v apk     >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo apk add --no-cache tmux
  elif command -v pacman  >/dev/null 2>&1; then sudo pacman -S --noconfirm tmux
  else echo "no supported package manager found"; fi
fi
tmux -V

snippets.name: Will this host keep my session alive?
snippets.description: Reports which multiplexer is installed, lists the sessions already running, and says what that means for a dropped connection.

steps.content:
# Voltius prefers tmux, falls back to screen, and warns when neither exists.
screen_ls() {
  if command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
    SCR_RC=$?
    if [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT"
    else
      echo "screen: no sessions"
    fi
  fi
}

for m in tmux screen; do
  if command -v "$m" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    case "$m" in
      tmux)   VER=$(tmux -V 2>&1 | head -1) ;;
      screen) VER=$(screen -v 2>&1 | head -1) ;;
    esac
    if [ -n "$VER" ]; then
      echo "$m: $VER"
    else
      echo "$m: installed (version not reported)"
    fi
  else
    echo "$m: not installed"
  fi
done

echo
echo "== Sessions on this host =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls

echo
if command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=> Your session survives a dropped connection (tmux)."
elif command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "=> Your session survives a dropped connection (screen)."
else
  echo "=> Nothing persistent here: a dropped connection kills the session."
  echo "   Install tmux to fix that."
fi

snippets.name: Kill a stale session
snippets.description: Lists your sessions, kills the one you name, then lists them again. A name that does not exist kills nothing.

steps.content:
# The list is printed before anything is killed, on purpose — kill the wrong
# session and you lose whatever was running inside it. Both kills below only
# fire on an exact name match: tmux and screen both do prefix matching by
# default, so an unanchored match could kill session "foobar" when you asked
# to kill "foo".
TARGET="{{session}}"

screen_ls() {
  if command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
    SCR_RC=$?
    if [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ]; then
      printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT"
    else
      echo "screen: no sessions"
    fi
  fi
}

# Exact-match check for screen: screen -S/-X quit prefix-matches like tmux
# does, and unlike tmux there is no "=name" anchor to force an exact match,
# so we parse `screen -ls` ourselves and only proceed on an exact hit.
screen_has_exact() {
  command -v screen >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 1
  SCR_OUT=$(screen -ls 2>/dev/null)
  SCR_RC=$?
  [ "$SCR_RC" -eq 0 ] && [ -n "$SCR_OUT" ] || return 1
  printf '%s\n' "$SCR_OUT" | awk -F'\t' -v t="$1" '
    NF >= 2 { id = $2; sub(/^[0-9]+\./, "", id); if (id == t) { found = 1; exit } }
    END { exit !found }
  '
}

echo "== Sessions before =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls

echo
echo "== Killing '$TARGET' =="
if tmux kill-session -t "=$TARGET" 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "killed tmux session $TARGET"
elif screen_has_exact "$TARGET" && screen -S "$TARGET" -X quit 2>/dev/null; then
  echo "killed screen session $TARGET"
else
  echo "no session named '$TARGET' — nothing killed"
fi

echo
echo "== Sessions after =="
command -v tmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && { tmux ls 2>/dev/null || echo "tmux: no sessions"; }
screen_ls
